recipe.title: Tomato, Mushroom & Mycoprotein Wholewheat Bolognese with Spinach and Vegetarian Parmesan-Style Cheese
recipe.description: A rich, high-protein wholewheat pasta bolognese with deeply browned mycoprotein and chestnut mushrooms, a reduced tomato sauce, wilted spinach and a savoury vegetarian Parmesan-style finish.

ingredients.purchase_notes: Use 300 g; retail pack size may vary. Check the package allergen declaration.
ingredients.preparation: Use chilled or fully defrosted according to the package instructions.
ingredients.notes: Choose plain vegetarian mince rather than a pre-sauced product. Formulations commonly contain egg.

ingredients.preparation: Brush or wipe clean rather than soaking.
Wash if required and dry thoroughly.

ingredients.purchase_notes: Use the entire contents of 1 approximately 400 g tin.

ingredients.notes: Whole onions do not scale perfectly for every serving quantity; round sensibly when scaling.

ingredients.preparation: Wash and peel only if the skin is coarse or damaged.
ingredients.notes: Whole carrots do not scale perfectly for every serving quantity; round sensibly when scaling.

ingredients.preparation: Peel before finely grating or crushing.

ingredients.notes: Added at the end so its acidity remains fresh and balances the reduced tomato sauce.

ingredients.purchase_notes: Use 25 g. Choose a vegetarian hard Italian-style cheese made without animal rennet; retail pack size may vary.

ingredients.notes: Use 1/4 tsp in the pasta water and 1/4 tsp in the sauce; mycoprotein and cheese contribute additional salt.

ingredients.purchase_notes: Use approximately 2 L for cooking the pasta; reserve approximately 100 ml of the pasta cooking water before draining.
ingredients.notes: Most of the pasta water is discarded after cooking.

equipment.notes: Use a broad pan so the mushrooms and mycoprotein can brown rather than steam.
Used to bring the pasta water to temperature quickly.
For garlic and vegetarian Parmesan-style cheese.
Used to coarsely grate the carrot quickly.
Used to reserve pasta cooking water.

mise_en_place.instruction: Peel the onion, trim the ends and dice the usable flesh into approximately 5 mm pieces. Trim the carrot and coarsely grate it. Peel and finely grate or crush the garlic. Trim the mushroom stem ends and slice the mushrooms approximately 5 mm thick.
mise_en_place.endpoint: The onion, carrot, garlic and mushrooms are prepared for rapid sequential cooking.

mise_en_place.instruction: Wash the spinach if required and dry thoroughly. Remove only unusually thick or damaged stems.
mise_en_place.endpoint: The spinach is clean and dry enough to wilt without unnecessarily watering the sauce.

mise_en_place.instruction: Finely grate the 25 g vegetarian Parmesan-style hard cheese.
mise_en_place.endpoint: The cheese is finely grated so a relatively small amount distributes evenly over both portions.

procedure.title: Brown the mushrooms
procedure.instruction: Heat the sauté pan over medium-high heat for approximately 1 minute. Add 1 tsp olive oil and the sliced mushrooms. Spread them into a broad layer and cook for approximately 5-7 minutes, stirring only every 60-90 seconds at first.
procedure.endpoint: The mushroom liquid has evaporated and the mushroom surfaces have distinct deep golden-brown patches.

corrective_actions.condition: The mushrooms release liquid and remain grey.
corrective_actions.action: Keep the pan uncovered at medium-high heat and avoid stirring until the visible liquid has evaporated.

corrective_actions.condition: The mushrooms darken before their released liquid evaporates.
corrective_actions.action: Reduce the heat slightly and continue until the pan is dry.

procedure.title: Cook the aromatics and brown the mycoprotein
procedure.instruction: Add the remaining 1 tsp olive oil, diced onion and grated carrot to the browned mushrooms. Cook for approximately 3-4 minutes until the onion begins to soften. Add the 300 g mycoprotein mince and 1/2 tsp black pepper, increase the heat to medium-high and cook for another 4-5 minutes, stirring only often enough to prevent catching.
procedure.endpoint: The onion is softened, the carrot has collapsed into the mixture and the mycoprotein has developed visible browned areas rather than remaining uniformly pale.

corrective_actions.condition: The mixture releases enough liquid to prevent browning.
corrective_actions.action: Keep the pan uncovered and continue at medium-high heat until the visible moisture evaporates before proceeding.

corrective_actions.condition: The onion or carrot begins catching before the mycoprotein has browned.
corrective_actions.action: Reduce the heat slightly and stir more frequently.

procedure.title: Cook the tomato purée and aromatics
procedure.instruction: Reduce the heat to medium. Add the garlic, 2 tbsp tomato purée and 1 tsp dried oregano. Stir continuously for approximately 1 minute, scraping the tomato purée across the pan base so it darkens slightly.
procedure.endpoint: The garlic and oregano smell aromatic and the tomato purée has darkened from bright red towards brick red without scorching.

corrective_actions.condition: The garlic or tomato purée begins catching or smelling bitter.
corrective_actions.action: Immediately add the chopped tomatoes and stir thoroughly.

procedure.title: Reduce the bolognese sauce
procedure.instruction: Add the 400 g chopped tomatoes and 1/4 tsp fine salt. Bring to a lively simmer, then cook uncovered over medium heat for approximately 8-10 minutes, stirring every 2-3 minutes.
procedure.endpoint: The sauce is thick and glossy, no watery tomato liquid separates around the edges, and a spatula drawn across the pan base leaves a trail visible for approximately 2 seconds.

corrective_actions.condition: The sauce begins sticking before reaching the reduction endpoint.
corrective_actions.action: Reduce the heat and add 1 tbsp of the reserved pasta water once available.

corrective_actions.condition: The sauce remains visibly watery after 10 minutes.
corrective_actions.action: Increase the heat slightly and continue uncovered until it passes the stated spatula-trail test.

procedure.title: Cook the wholewheat spaghetti
procedure.instruction: While the tomato sauce reduces, boil approximately 2 L water in the kettle and transfer it to the saucepan. Return to a vigorous boil, add 1/4 tsp fine salt and the 130 g wholewheat spaghetti. Cook according to the lower end of the package timing, normally approximately 8-10 minutes, stirring well after the pasta first enters the water.
procedure.endpoint: The spaghetti is tender through the centre but retains a slight bite and is not soft or swollen.

corrective_actions.condition: The spaghetti reaches the correct texture before the stated package time.
corrective_actions.action: Proceed immediately to reserving cooking water and draining rather than continuing to cook by the clock.

procedure.title: Reserve pasta water and drain
procedure.instruction: Before draining, scoop approximately 100 ml pasta cooking water into the measuring jug. Drain the spaghetti thoroughly in the colander. Do not rinse it.
procedure.endpoint: The spaghetti is well drained but retains its surface starch, and approximately 100 ml hot cooking water is reserved for sauce adjustment.

procedure.title: Wilt the spinach and balance the sauce
procedure.instruction: Add the spinach to the reduced sauce in 2 additions, folding each portion through until wilted. Cook for approximately 1-2 minutes, then remove the pan from the heat and stir through 2 tsp red wine vinegar.
procedure.endpoint: The spinach is fully wilted, the sauce remains thick and glossy, and the vinegar gives a clean acidic lift without making the sauce taste sharply vinegary.

corrective_actions.condition: The spinach releases enough water to loosen the sauce.
corrective_actions.action: Return the pan to medium-high heat for 1-2 minutes and reduce until the original thick consistency returns.

procedure.title: Coat the spaghetti in the bolognese
procedure.instruction: Add the drained spaghetti to the bolognese sauce and toss thoroughly over low heat for approximately 1 minute. Add reserved pasta water 1 tbsp at a time only if required to make the sauce cling evenly to the spaghetti.
procedure.endpoint: Every strand of spaghetti is coated in the thick tomato-mushroom sauce, with no watery liquid at the bottom of the pan and no dry clumps of pasta.

corrective_actions.condition: The sauce is too thick to coat the spaghetti evenly.
corrective_actions.action: Add 1 tbsp reserved pasta water, toss thoroughly and repeat only if required.

corrective_actions.condition: The sauce becomes loose after adding pasta water.
corrective_actions.action: Continue tossing over medium heat for approximately 1 minute until the excess moisture evaporates.

plating.instruction: Divide the wholewheat spaghetti and bolognese evenly between two warm bowls. Scatter half of the finely grated vegetarian Parmesan-style cheese over each serving and serve immediately while the sauce is glossy and the cheese is freshly melting.

storage.storage_instructions: Cool leftovers promptly and refrigerate in a sealed container for up to 2 days. The bolognese sauce without pasta may be frozen for up to 1 month. For the best texture, freeze sauce separately and cook fresh pasta after defrosting.
reheating_methods: Hob: place leftover pasta and sauce in a covered sauté pan over low-medium heat with 1-2 tbsp water and heat, stirring regularly, until piping hot throughout.
Oven: place in a covered ovenproof dish with 1-2 tbsp water and heat at approximately 180°C until piping hot throughout.
For frozen sauce, defrost safely in the refrigerator, then reheat on the hob until piping hot before combining with freshly cooked pasta.

either_retailer: Vegetarian mycoprotein mince — 1 pack; use 300 g.
Wholewheat spaghetti — 1 pack; use 130 g dry.
Canned chopped tomatoes — 1 approximately 400 g tin.
Vegetarian Parmesan-style hard cheese — 1 pack; use 25 g.

restaurant_quality_features: Mushrooms are browned until their released liquid has completely evaporated, creating substantial savoury depth.
Mycoprotein is allowed to brown before the tomato sauce is added rather than simply simmering from the start.
Tomato purée is cooked directly against the pan to deepen and sweeten its flavour.
The tomato sauce is reduced to a glossy consistency before spinach and pasta are introduced.
Red wine vinegar added after reduction preserves a fresh acidic lift.
Starchy pasta cooking water is used only as required to help the reduced sauce cling to the wholewheat spaghetti.
Finely grated vegetarian Parmesan-style cheese provides concentrated savoury richness without requiring a large quantity.
nutrition_notes: Approximately 605 kcal and 43 g protein per serving.
Mycoprotein provides the principal protein contribution, supported by wholewheat pasta and vegetarian hard cheese.
Wholewheat spaghetti, mushrooms, spinach, carrot and tomato contribute substantial dietary fibre.
A large vegetable and mushroom proportion adds volume and flavour without relying on excessive oil.
Nutrition values are estimates and will vary with the exact mycoprotein, pasta and vegetarian cheese products used.
critical_success_factors: Brown the mushrooms until their released moisture has evaporated before adding the remaining sauce ingredients.
Allow the mycoprotein to develop visible browning rather than steaming it in a wet pan.
Cook the tomato purée briefly before adding canned tomatoes.
Reduce the bolognese until it passes the stated spatula-trail test.
Do not overcook the wholewheat spaghetti.
Add pasta water gradually and only as required so the final sauce remains thick and clings to the pasta.
Add the red wine vinegar at the end to preserve fresh acidity.
